summary: Vinod Kumar Roy is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Patna University, the University of Delhi, and Magadh University, where he became an Assistant Professor (Senior Scale) in 2019.

Vinod Mishra is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Kurukshetra University and completed his Ph.D. at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya. He became a Professor at the Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering and Technology in 2010.
Vipul Jadav is an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. in Sanskrit from Shree Somnath Sanskrit University (2017–2021). He was appointed Assistant Professor at the same university in 2020.
Virchand Gandhi (1864–1901) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai (~1880–1884) and taught Herbert Warren.
Virendra Kumar Varma worked in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He studied under traditional teachers Ramnath Dixit and Gopal Chandra Mishra, and he taught Kamala Prasad Tripathi.
Virendra Kumar Verma worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under teachers Ramanatha Dikshita and Gopal Chandra Mishra, and he taught Kamala Prasad Mishra.

Virendra Nath Misra (1935–2015) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Lucknow and Savitribai Phule Pune University, and served as Director of Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1990–2000).

Indologist Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar (1887–1943) studied at St. Xavier's, St John's, Edinburgh, and Berlin under Heinrich Lüders, Hermann Jacobi, and Moriz Winternitz. He served with the Archaeological Survey of India and as General Editor of the Mahabharata (1925).

Vishva Bandhu (1897–1973), an Indologist and linguist, studied under Alfred Cooper Woolner. He served as Founder-Principal of Dayanand Brahma Mahavidyalaya (1921), Director of DAV College Lahore (1934), and Director of the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute (~1934–1973).

Vishvanath Narayan Mandlik (1833–1899) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Elphinstone College. He served as Vice-President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and was an examiner at the University of Mumbai.

Vishwa Nath Pathak (1926–2003) was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He served as a Professor at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1973–1978 and 1987).

Vishwanath Prasad Varma (b. 1924) works in philosophy and Indology. He studied under Dhirendra Mohan Datta, Ganga Nath Bhattacharya, Joachim Wach, and doctoral supervisor Kali Kinkar Datta (~1947–1950).

Indologist Vishwanathan Venkatachalam (1925–2002) studied at Madras, Nagpur, and Vikram universities. He held multiple academic posts, including Director of Scindia Oriental Institute, Professor at Vikram University, and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University.

Vitalij Petrovič Furnika (1940–1993) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Semën Gesselevič Rudin and completed his education at Saint Petersburg State University (1965–1970) and the University of Madras (1969–1970).

Vittore Pisani (1899–1990) was an Italian linguist and Indologist who studied at Sapienza University of Rome under Carlo Formichi and Antonino Pagliaro. He held academic posts at Rome, Florence, Cagliari, Università Cattolica, Bocconi, and Milan (1938–1969).
Vittorio Bettei worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as a teacher of Latin and Greek at Liceo Ginnasio Benedetto Cairoli and Liceo Canova.

Vittorio Rocca (1862–1905) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Pisa. He later held posts as a docent at Sapienza University of Rome and obtained a libera docenza in Sanskrit at Pisa in 1905.

Indologist Vitus Angermeier studied at the University of Vienna under Karin Preisendanz, Chlodwig H. Werba, and Roque Mesquita. He held posts as a Lecturer at the University of Vienna and as a Researcher/Project Leader at the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Vlad Bănățeanu (1900–1963) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Chernivtsi, Bucharest, EPHE, and INALCO under Meillet, Benveniste, Ernout, Vendryes, Bloch, and Finot. He held posts at Chernivtsi University (1932) and the University of Bucharest.

Vladimir Aleksandrovich Chernyshev (1927–1999) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Moscow State University (~1948–1953) and held posts at the Moscow State Institute of International Relations (1952–1956) and the Institute of Oriental Studies (from 1956).
